clue.text: Gretna Green minister maybe having to fix round vessel with muscle

indicators.note: the binding word goes round the next pieces, enclosing them as a band would

parts.note: to bind something is to fix it fast
an urn is a vase or vessel
thew is an old word for muscle or sinew

explanation.surface: A clergyman at the Scottish wedding village builds up his strength and mends a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: BURN-THE-WIND is Scots for a blacksmith; the Gretna Green smith famously married eloping couples over his anvil, so he acted as a 'minister'.
explanation.definitionFit: Runaway couples at Gretna Green, a Scottish border village, were wed by the local smith, so this Scots word for a smith names that unofficial officiant.

clue.text: US conservative, only less intense

parts.note: but can mean only, as in 'but a child'
something toned down is made milder

explanation.surface: An American right-winger, just a bit milder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only' looks like a qualifier on the conservative, but it is the word but.
explanation.definitionFit: Buttoned-down, from the button-down collar, is American slang for staid and conventional in outlook.

clue.text: Sailor's block aloft, fellow holding half of rope

parts.note: aloft means up high

indicators.note: holding means the man's word grips the other letters inside

parts.note: he, the male pronoun, stands for a fellow

indicators.note: half of a word is just its first two letters here

parts.note: first half of the word

explanation.surface: A seaman's pulley hung up high, with a man gripping some rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aloft' sits with the block as if it were where the block hangs, but it supplies UP.
explanation.definitionFit: An uphroe, or euphroe, is a long wooden block with holes through which the lines of an awning's crowfoot are rove.

clue.text: I've edible seeds put out with number coming round (7, two words)

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters are rearranged
coming round means one word goes round the other

parts.note: nine is a number
the three letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tree announces its tasty seeds as numbers are put out.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue speaks as the tree: 'I've edible seeds'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nut pine is any pine, such as the stone pine, whose large seeds are eaten as pine nuts.

clue.text: What ends in debauchery becomes No. 1 for e.g. famed musketeers?

indicators.note: the word's closing letter is the one that moves
becoming number one means moving to first place, the front of the word

parts.note: riot means wild revelry, as in 'run riot'

explanation.surface: A tale of debauched swordsmen and their leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of RIOT becomes number one, giving TRIO. Dumas's Three Musketeers are Athos, Porthos and Aramis.
explanation.definitionFit: The Three Musketeers are a famous group of three, and a trio is any set of three.

clue.text: 'She is wobbly soprano,' with which her detractors greet her

definitions.text: 'She is wobbly soprano,' with which her detractors greet her

indicators.note: wobbly means unsteady, so the letters shake into a new order

parts.note: these letters are rearranged
S is the abbreviation for soprano in music

explanation.surface: Critics jeer at a singer with a shaky high voice.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: an anagram of SHE IS plus S, and the noise an audience makes at an unsteady soprano.
explanation.definitionFit: Hisses are the sibilant sounds of disapproval an audience makes at a performer it dislikes.

clue.text: River, absolute end of glacier, forms this sandy ridge

parts.note: the Esk is a river in Scotland and northern England
A is a standard abbreviation for absolute

indicators.note: end of means the final letter of the next word

parts.note: closing letter

explanation.surface: Where a river meets the edge of a glacier, a sandy bank builds up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absolute end' reads as one idea, but absolute gives A and end applies only to glacier.
explanation.definitionFit: An eskar, or esker, is a long winding ridge of sand and gravel laid down by a stream under a glacier.

clue.text: We were flat out, score once imbibed, blotto (8, two words)

indicators.note: something imbibed is taken inside, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: lying flat, we lay
law is an obsolete Scots word for a tavern score or reckoning

explanation.surface: We passed out, having drunk too much to pay the old tab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' here is a drinker's tab, not a tally of points; the old word survives in Scots lawing, a tavern bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Well away is British slang for very drunk, the same state as blotto.

clue.text: Take in nothing that is knotty

indicators.note: in places one item inside the next

parts.note: nil means nothing
R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions
i.e. is the abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: A problem nobody can absorb is a tough one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take in' looks like one phrase meaning absorb, but take is R and in is the insertion. NIRLIE is Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirlie is a Scots word for knotty or stunted, describing something gnarled and shrivelled.

clue.text: What a Gambian earns when cutting tropical tree

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: the dali is a tropical American tree whose seeds yield wax
as can mean when

explanation.surface: How much a West African worker earns from felling trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The dalasi is the currency of the Gambia, so it is the money a Gambian is paid in.

clue.text: One who takes delight in his cups gets involved in gross … this?

definitions.text: One who takes delight in his cups gets involved in gross … this?

indicators.note: getting involved in something means going inside it

parts.note: gross can mean fat or fleshy

parts.words: One who takes delight in his cups
parts.note: a craftsman who makes cups would delight in them

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker sinks into grossness and wonders if this is the result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His cups' suggests drink, but the man who delights in cups is the one who makes them. The whole clue also defines it: a drinker's gross indulgence.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleshpottery is luxurious, self-indulgent living, from the fleshpots of Egypt, the kind of excess a hard drinker falls into.

clue.text: A pull I misjudged holding climber in several rows

indicators.note: a thing misjudged has been got wrong, so these letters come out in the wrong order
holding means gripping something inside, so the jumbled letters wrap round another word

parts.note: these six letters are rearranged
a riser is one who rises or climbs

explanation.surface: Someone tugging badly while holding a mountaineer roped between several others.
explanation.walkthrough: PLURISERIAL is a botanical term for parts arranged in more than one row.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin prefix pluri- means many and serial refers to rows or series, so the word describes an arrangement in multiple ranks.

clue.text: Yon roofing specialist's not dear

indicators.note: not tells us a word is to be left out of the longer one

parts.note: a thatcher roofs houses with straw or reed
French for dear

explanation.surface: Someone over there who roofs houses does not charge much.
explanation.walkthrough: THATCHER minus the French CHER leaves THAT. 'Not dear' looks like 'cheap', but it is an instruction to drop a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Yon is an old or dialect demonstrative meaning that one over there, the same pointing word as the answer.

clue.text: Heraldic border? Bed Richard tricked out with this possibly

indicators.note: tricked out means dressed up or rearranged, so the letters of the phrase are reworked
possibly signals one possible rearrangement of the letters
the clue's own answer is the part left over once the named words are taken out of the rearranged phrase

parts.note: the whole opening phrase is the letter pool
these letters account for most of the pool

explanation.surface: A puzzled designer wonders whether a bed called Richard might be decorated with a coat-of-arms edging.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of 'Heraldic border' equal BED RICHARD plus the answer, so removing BED RICHARD leaves ORLE.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry an orle is a narrow band running round a shield inside its edge, a kind of inner border.

clue.text: Successful Cambridge examinees love taking part in jaunts

indicators.note: a thing taking part in something goes into its middle

parts.note: trips are short outings
love is nil, the letter O

explanation.surface: Students who passed at Cambridge enjoy romance on their outings.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tripos is the Cambridge University honours exam; Chambers also uses the word for the list of those who passed it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripos can mean the class list of candidates who have passed the Cambridge honours examination, so it names those successful students.

clue.text: Groups of feathers sadly including regular parts of quill

indicators.note: including means the outer word holds the selected letters inside it

parts.note: alas is said sadly

indicators.note: regular parts means letters taken at even intervals, every other one

parts.note: second and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: Bunches of plumes, sadly including a few bits of a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: An alula is the bastard wing, the small tuft of feathers on a bird's thumb, so the plural names such feather clusters.

clue.text: Manure fruit tree

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to dress land with a calcium fertiliser
second meaning: the tree bearing small green citrus fruits

explanation.surface: A gardener's shorthand: put dung round the fruit tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Manure is a verb here: farmers spread the white powder on fields to sweeten the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a soil dressing spread by farmers and a citrus tree, so each half stands alone.

clue.text: American tinsmith maybe joined a border

parts.note: met means came together
taken as written
a list is an edge or selvage of cloth

explanation.surface: A US metalworker teamed up with a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: METALIST is the American spelling of metallist, with one L.
explanation.definitionFit: A metallist is a worker in metals, and a tinsmith is one example; American spelling drops an L.

clue.text: It adds a touch of redness to a meal

definitions.text: It adds a touch of redness to a meal

indicators.note: a touch of means only a small bit, here the very first letter

parts.note: opening letter
a meal is a dish

explanation.surface: Something that gives a dinner a little colour.
explanation.walkthrough: R joined to A DISH spells the answer, and the whole clue also defines it: the red-skinned root brightens a salad.
explanation.definitionFit: The small red-skinned root is sliced into salads and garnishes, adding a dab of colour to the plate.

clue.text: Novel quality making publishing imprint leader in style

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, which is added on here

parts.note: George Newnes was a British publisher whose name became an imprint
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A publisher deciding what gives a book its originality and stylish lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book, but it is the adjective new; Newnes was a British publishing house, famous for Tit-Bits and The Strand Magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Being novel means being new, so the quality of a novel thing is freshness or newness.

clue.text: Identify startling utterance in the vespers

parts.note: to place someone is to identify them
bo is an exclamation used to startle

explanation.surface: Recognising a shocking outburst during evening prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The vespers' wants evensong, but it is the specific vespers of the Office for the Dead, which opens with the word placebo.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman Catholic rite, Placebo is the name given to vespers for the dead, after its first antiphon.

clue.text: Somebody putting a pound on Hail Mary

parts.note: a quid is British slang for a pound sterling
the initials of Ave Maria, Latin for Hail Mary

explanation.surface: A punter betting a pound on a desperate last-gasp chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hail Mary' suggests a long-shot bet, but it is the prayer Ave Maria, AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Quidam is Latin for a certain person, used in English for an unnamed individual or somebody.

clue.text: Gold-leaf for mould removed from casing and hammered out

indicators.note: metal hammered out is beaten into a new shape, so the letters are reshaped
with its casing removed a phrase loses its outer letters

parts.note: the two words run together

explanation.surface: Gilt for a mould, freed from its case and beaten flat.
explanation.walkthrough: Lose the outer F and D of 'for mould' and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Ormolu is gold or gilded bronze used for decoration, originally ground gold leaf, French or moulu.

clue.text: Bit of coal-tar in mixture on what besiegers launched?

indicators.note: in places the chosen letter inside the following word

parts.note: a salad is a mixture

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small part of it, here its first letter

parts.note: opening letter
o' is a shortened form of on, as in Chambers

explanation.surface: A chemist adds coal-tar to a mixture and wonders what the attackers fired.
explanation.walkthrough: S(C)ALAD + O. A scalado is an assault in which ladders are set against the walls, so besiegers launched one rather than fired it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalado, like escalade, is an attack scaling fortress walls by ladder, an assault an army mounts during a siege.

clue.text: Worries about small time for bills

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round another

parts.note: cares are worries
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Fretting briefly over the bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' asks for the abbreviation of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A carte is a bill of fare, a menu card, so cartes are bills in that sense.

clue.text: Denies upsetting poet's plan

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over and disturbing, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to go along with an upsetting scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' marks a Spenserian spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Desine is Edmund Spenser's spelling of design, used as a noun for a plan or scheme.

clue.text: Composition of Edmund Rubbra may leave this audience numbed

indicators.note: a composition puts its material together afresh, so the letters of the name are rearranged
leave means what remains once the named word is taken away

parts.note: the composer's name is the letter pool
taken as written and removed from the pool

explanation.surface: A dull piece by the English composer Edmund Rubbra leaves the concert-goers numb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audience' wants to mean listeners, but it is the formal reception sense. Rearranged, EDMUND RUBBRA is the answer plus NUMBED.
explanation.definitionFit: A durbar was a formal reception held by an Indian ruler or British viceroy, an audience in the sense of a ceremonial hearing.

clue.text: Fine actors will thrill fan so with these 'meaty' parts

indicators.note: to thrill is to excite and stir up, so the letters are mixed
the answer is what remains from the mixed letters beyond the plain words given

parts.note: the two words are the letter pool
taken as written and removed from the pool

explanation.surface: Good actors will excite fans with juicy roles.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: 'Fine actors' rearranged is FAN SO plus the answer. 'Meaty' parts look like juicy roles but are muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: Recti are straight muscles, such as those of the abdomen, and muscle is the meat of the body.

clue.text: Nurse, one given a merry dance round

parts.note: a, the indefinite article, means one

indicators.note: turned round means the dance's name is read back to front

parts.note: the hay is a lively old country dance

explanation.surface: A nurse leads a patient a merry dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given a merry dance' looks like the idiom for being led astray; here the dance is a real one, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An ayah is a nursemaid or children's nurse in India and other former colonies.

clue.text: Dale, say, member of broadcasting family dropping by

indicators.note: dropping means letting fall, so a short word is shed

parts.note: Richard Dimbleby and his sons David and Jonathan are famous BBC presenters
taken as written and removed

explanation.surface: A TV presenter named Dale belongs to a broadcasting dynasty and pops in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dale' looks like a name but is a valley. The Dimblebys are a British family of broadcasters.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimble is a dialect word for a dell or wooded hollow, and a dale is a valley, so 'say' marks it as an example.

clue.text: One lacking in caritas, possibly?

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible arrangement of the remaining letters
lacking in means a letter is missing from the word that follows

parts.note: a means one
Latin for charity or love

explanation.surface: A puzzle about someone who lacks Christian charity.
explanation.walkthrough: CARITAS without one A, rearranged; the whole clue is the definition, since a bigot lacks love for his neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Caritas is love of all humankind, and a person prejudiced against other races fails at exactly that charity.

clue.text: Bearing north of Tay initially, lost motorist may ask for this

definitions.text: lost motorist may ask for this

parts.note: an air is a manner or bearing

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: opening letter

explanation.surface: A driver lost somewhere north of the River Tay in Scotland needs a compass bearing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'north of' means placed above, so AIR comes before T. AIRT is a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Airt is Scots for a direction or point of the compass, which a lost driver would ask for.

clue.text: Party in Oregon achieving repute locally?

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the second

parts.note: OR is the US postal abbreviation for the state
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Throwing a party in Oregon to become famous in the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locally' means as spelt in Oregon: the American spelling of odour, as in being in good odour, well thought of.
explanation.definitionFit: Odour can mean repute or standing, as in good or bad odour, and Americans spell it without the u.

clue.text: Steamer circles this lake in sequence

indicators.note: circles means goes round, so one word encloses the answer

parts.note: a series is things in sequence
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A paddle-steamer goes round a lake in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the inner part of a longer word: the clue defines the whole, and the steamer's letters wrap round the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Erie is one of the five Great Lakes, on the border of the United States and Canada.

clue.text: One result of air pollution, alders went terribly black inside

indicators.note: inside places the colour's letter within the mixed letters
terribly suggests something has gone badly wrong, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the trees' name is part of the letter pool
taken as written, also in the pool
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: Smog turned the alder trees dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went' looks like a verb joining the sentence but belongs to the letter pool. WALDSTERBEN is German for forest death, taken into English.
explanation.definitionFit: Waldsterben is the dying-back of forests blamed on acid rain and other airborne pollutants.

clue.text: Car park nervous t-tiros'll get stuck in without horns

indicators.note: a nervous person is jittery and unsettled, so the letters are shaken up
to get stuck in is to be lodged inside something

parts.note: muley describes hornless cattle
the stammered word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stammering novice drivers will end up jammed in a car park.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter t-tiros supplies the extra T. Muley (hornless) is mainly a US and dialect word for a polled cow.
explanation.definitionFit: A multistorey is a car park built on several levels, the noun short for multistorey car park.
